authority: Root explicitly confirmed registered publisher/root fixed templates and own reference/session descriptors supply immutable pins; arbitrary callers are outside this correctness boundary.
clarification: R02 uses unchanged root-registered pins while changing a candidate-owned temporary target byte or attempting a foreign path under those unchanged pins. A code identity error must precede execution of the changed target.

R05 changes a foreign reference or session_path while retaining the fixed registered code/session-directory and own-session binding. A different registered generic session can legitimately be constructed by its own publisher; this is not a global filesystem isolation claim.
No claim forbids arbitrary out-of-protocol callers from recomputing digests or changing all bindings. Such caller-provided digests are not publisher authentication.
Static author templates keep REQUEST/reference/code/session and runtime/launcher source exact; only the declared closed VIEW/CONFIRM fields are author edits.

registration_required_before_execution: Candidate API/runtime/reader/legacy and source-literal file refs
Exact Python/Node versions and pinned paths
Root authorization for source-only generic controls
harness_plan.draft_interface: compact_protocol.py code_bindings, session_path, runtime_command, runtime_*_template and REQUEST_FORMAT; direct runtime invocations use exact closed canonical JSON
harness_plan.execution_guard: No import of candidate executable API, no process/model/VIEW or fixture setup until source registration authenticates candidate+harness files and explicit controls_authorized true
harness_plan.fresh_state: Two separate run directories; each control creates its own carrier/session with unrelated generic data.
harness_plan.process_observations: Actual Popen PID, exact integer returncode, argv or fixed shell command, stdout/stderr raw byte files and refs. Hidden nested PID unavailable unless exposed.
harness_plan.synthetic_pending: Synthetic-control chunk_id and native-like result envelope constructed from actual generic process stdout/status; explicitly labeled synthetic and not native tool attestation.
